title: Graphing the Absolute Value of a Quadratic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = |x^2 - 4| by writing it without absolute value bars, and identify its zeros, its local maximum, and the behavior of its arms.
finalAnswer: y = \begin{cases} x^2 - 4, & |x| \ge 2 \\ 4 - x^2, & |x| < 2 \end{cases} \quad \text{zeros at } x = \pm 2,\ \text{local max at } (0, 4)

steps.title: Split at the sign change of the inside
steps.explanation: Outside the roots the quadratic is already nonnegative, so the bars do nothing; between -2 and 2 the quadratic is negative, so the graph there is the flipped parabola 4 - x^2.
steps.why: Absolute value acts as the identity on nonnegative output and as a reflection on negative output, which is the whole transformation rule.

steps.title: List the visible features
steps.explanation: The curve touches the axis at x = -2 and x = 2, rises to a hump with peak (0, 4) between them, and leaves as two upward arms like the original parabola.
steps.why: The reflected hump creates a local maximum that does not exist for y = x^2 - 4, which is why the picture changes qualitatively.

steps.title: Check corners and choose a window
steps.explanation: The two pieces meet at x = plus or minus 2 with one-sided slopes of opposite sign, so the joined curve has sharp corners there; the window [-4, 4] by [-1, 12] shows the hump plus the start of both arms.
steps.why: Knowing the corners are non-differentiable explains why the curve looks kinked there even in a smooth software render.
